title: Export Control Amendment (Banning Cotton Exports to Ensure Water Security) Bill 2019 [No. 2]
short_title: Export Control Amendment (Banning Cotton Exports to Ensure Water Security) Bill 2019 [No. 2]

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would prohibit exports of cotton grown anywhere in Australia after a transition period, by amending the existing export control framework for prescribed goods.
It would treat Australian-grown cotton as prescribed goods and deem an absolute export prohibition to apply after the stated three-year lead-in under the new section.
The legislation would commence the day after royal assent, while cotton production for use within Australia would remain outside the proposed export ban.
changes: Australian-grown cotton would enter the prescribed-goods category under export control law.
The export ban would apply nationally, rather than only to cotton grown in the Murray-Darling Basin.
Prohibited exports would fall under the existing offence carrying a maximum of five years’ imprisonment.
summary.affected: Australian cotton growers and cotton exporters are affected.
